chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a man performing Tamattu', what should he do? He said: 'He intends the Tamattu' and enters into Ihram with Hajj.' From Abu Basir, he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who stipulates in Hajj that 'You release me where you detained me,' is the Hajj upon him for next year? He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: How does one perform the ritual intention and Ihram for Tamattu' Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the technical requirement for Tamattu' pilgrims to explicitly intend the Hajj while in the state of Ihram, distinguishing it from the Umrah Ihram. It further establishes the validity of conditional stipulations (shart) in Hajj rituals, where a pilgrim can specify the location of their release from Ihram constraints, ensuring the ritual's completeness for the subsequent year. These details reflect the Shia emphasis on precise intention (niyyah) and the flexibility of legal conditions within ritual worship.
